newsitem.title: USA: Snows blankets central U.S. plains.
newsitem.headline: Snows blankets central U.S. plains.

text.p: A winter storm moved into Missouri and Illinois on Friday, a day after it snarled traffic and shut schools and businesses in Kansas.

The brunt of the storm's snow hit on Thursday in central Kansas, with as much as seven inches (18 cm) reported in some areas. Authorities said the weather played a role in at least three traffic deaths across the state.
"It is one of our more significant snows of the winter," John Eichkorn, spokesman for the Kansas Highway Patrol, said.
Winter weather advisories and warnings went into effect on Thursday night in Missouri as snow, sleet and freezing rain bore down on the state from the southwest.

Joel Burgio, a meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. in Springfield, Massachusetts, said a narrow band of snow would likely drop two to four inches (five-10 cm) on Friday from central Missouri into southern Illinois and Indiana.
Burgio said the same low pressure system would track across the lower Mississippi valley, bringing steady rains to Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Tennessee.
